/u/aelendel {Ph.D | Geology | Paleobiology}:

There is a serious problem with this article.

The major mass extinctions are measured from looking back.

Declaring that we are in one, especially in the early stages, is just simply not possible. You can't take an instaneous rate, project it forward for tens of thousands of years, and declare that it will stay that way for LONGER THAN OUR CIVILIZATION HAS EXISTED. It's insane and yet, that's what they are doing here.

Background extinction rates aren't an instantaneous constant rate. "Background" extinction includes period of low rates and period of high rates. The PETM, as an example, had a significant turnover, was caused by global climate change larger than what we are predicting-- and ALSO wasn't above the background extinction rate as measured.

Anyways, bad public reporting on what is fundamentally an important topic.

Well this is effectively an animal shelter for dogs that no one adopts and even though her life savings is going into this she chooses not to euthanize them. There are plenty of situations smaller than this that a lot of people rose up against, so why not now? I'm against abolishing this entirely because they're in the same way as chickens and cows, using dogs as a source of food, and that's their deal their culture/tradition etc but there's no reason to start stealing dogs belonging to other people and torturing them all the way along until they're dead.

I just wonder how much of that $5000 in funding is going towards her travel costs \ accommodation. Don't get me wrong, I really applaud what she is doing, but I would like to know that it is the most effective use of my money should I donate. Quite frankly, I am very dubious of many charities \ causes that actually end up giving a small amount to the cause with the rest going on overheads. Sure it is a worthy cause, but I would rather give money to established more transparent campaigns and in this case surely it would make sense to support local campaigns in China (if there are any).

I'm not against the eating of dogs - personally I am, but I also understand that people eat different things in different cultures and I can't just go imposing what my values are upon them. What's unacceptable about this is the fact that some of these dogs are stolen from their owners, skinned and boiled alive and beaten as well. This festival isn't viewed as a good thing in China as well. The torture part of this festival is what concerns me the most. In 2011 the Chinese were able to rise up against this practice and stop the festival since the majority of them don't support it, but even then since there was no "major" government intervention, nothing happened. If the government were able to inspect the dogs and somehow make sure that they weren't pets or tortured that would be a different story.

If not donating money, then how about raising more awareness about this? Awareness about what goes on is definitely an effective tool if done correctly.

Recently China made some policies that would bar their people from traveling to other countries if they exhibited bad behavior. Why did they do it? Because there was a media storm against them, people from the countries they were visiting began posting videos of them doing stuff like cutting lines, defaming sacred places and overall bad behavior(one even threw hot noodles at a flight attendant in an argument) and this gave china an extremely bad image to the point where the government saw no other solution except barring them from travel and having those who do travel take some seminars about proper behavior when traveling. Awareness definitely goes a long way.

As for the lady, simply sharing the story can go a long way. You never know what you can accomplish and change unless you try. Realistically it should be impossible for one person to cut down a mountain but it was done. It should be impossible for a single person to plant a forest but it was done with persistence and determination. I disagree with your finishing statement about what realistically she can achieve, because the potential of what a single human being can do to change the way people think and the world is too large for most people to comprehend.

And if anyone reading this just thinks "meh it doesn't concern me" that's okay too because different people are passionate about different things, but this story is something I care about and I'm sure many others are as well if I'm unable to take any action beyond this post, I'll at least know that I did something I believed in and tried instead of shrugging it off. I got people to stop, read the article and think about this for a second and what it means. That to me, though small, is a victory.
